# Phase 1 — Configuration

## Purpose

Build and validate the JCR configuration needed by every later phase. The configuration is the controlled description of:

- the 14 Jockey Club racecourses;
- each course's maps and disciplines;
- the waypoints on each map;
- the sections and zones associated with those waypoints;
- available KML geometry and its quality;
- the identifiers needed to join Hub data, GoingStick data, weather stations and reports.

This phase is complete only when later analysis can use configuration identifiers rather than course-name or map-name guesses.

## Prerequisite: import the Going Reports

The map SVGs required for waypoint and zone matching are associated with Going Reports. SVG handling must therefore follow a complete Going Report import rather than relying on the planned fixture calendar alone.

Before the configuration inventory is run:

- import all available Going Reports for the selected analysis period from TT Hub;
- retain report identifiers, map identifiers, report dates and source provenance;
- retain report SVG references for waypoints and zones where available;
- record report import status, errors and duplicate or superseded reports;
- make the imported reports available to the SVG discovery step below.

The import is read-only against TT Hub and should write a local, versioned cache. A missing Going Report must be recorded as an exception; it must not be silently treated as a missing map or missing SVG.

Deliverable: imported Going Report cache and an import-status report, including the number of reports available per course, map and year.

## Working status

| Item | Current status |
|---|---|
| Phase | Phase 1 |
| Overall status | Step 1 complete; Phase 1 configuration in progress |
| Scope | Jockey Club racecourses; Cheltenham is the first detailed course |
| Analysis period | 2021–2025 initially; 2026 may be added as a partial year |
| Primary output | Versioned JCR configuration and validation report |

## Principles

1. A course may have one or more maps.
2. A map is the analytical unit for GoingStick spatial interpretation.
3. A waypoint belongs to a map and is not assumed to be globally unique.
4. Sections and zones are separate entities.
5. Zone membership is many-to-many: zones may overlap and a waypoint may belong to multiple zones.
6. Flat and jumps are map disciplines, not assumptions derived only from the racecourse name.
7. KML is supporting spatial evidence; its absence must not prevent non-spatial analysis.
8. Every imported identifier and every manually resolved mapping must retain provenance.

# Phase steps

## 1. Define the JCR course scope

Create the controlled course register from the current Jockey Club scope:

| Course | Hub ID | Canonical name | Alias | Maps | Waypoints | Included |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Aintree | 1 | Aintree | — | 3 | 324 | yes |
| Carlisle | 9 | Carlisle | — | 3 | 105 | yes |
| Cheltenham | 12 | Cheltenham | — | 20 | 1,113 | yes |
| Exeter | 17 | Exeter | — | 1 | 60 | yes |
| Epsom Downs | 16 | Epsom Downs | — | 8 | 487 | yes |
| Haydock Park | 23 | Haydock Park | — | 7 | 349 | yes |
| Huntingdon | 26 | Huntingdon | — | 2 | 72 | yes |
| Kempton Park | 28 | Kempton Park | — | 2 | 140 | yes |
| Market Rasen | 32 | Market Rasen | Mkt Rasen* | 1 | 32 | yes |
| Newmarket | 36 | Newmarket | — | 18 | 1,612 | yes |
| Nottingham | 38 | Nottingham | — | 1 | 32 | yes |
| Sandown Park | 45 | Sandown Park | — | 7 | 589 | yes |
| Warwick | 53 | Warwick | — | 2 | 66 | yes |
| Wincanton | 55 | Wincanton | — | 1 | 30 | yes |

Tasks:

- retrieve Hub course IDs and canonical names;
- record alternative names and historical names;
- record country and race discipline where available;
- flag courses with no maps or ambiguous identity;
- nominate Cheltenham as the first detailed-course test case.

Deliverable: `data/config/jcr_courses.parquet` and a source/provenance table.

### Step 1 result

Step 1 was run on 8 October 2026 against the read-only TT Hub connection. The [Jockey Club racecourse register](https://www.thejockeyclub.co.uk/about-us/our-present/racecourses/) and TT Hub matched all 14 courses by canonical name. The extract contains 14 courses, 76 maps and 5,011 configured waypoints. All courses are recorded as England in TT Hub. Market Rasen has the Hub alias `Mkt Rasen*`.

The Hub `no_maps` flag is set for nine courses even though map records are present. This is retained as a configuration warning for Step 2 rather than being interpreted as evidence that the courses have no maps.

Generated outputs:

- `data/config/jcr_courses.parquet`
- `data/config/jcr_course_provenance.parquet`
- `data/config/jcr_course_scope_report.json`


## 2. Inventory maps and map identity

For every JCR course, inventory all maps from the Hub map and track tables.

| Field | Required meaning |
|---|---|
| `course_id` | Stable Hub course identifier |
| `map_id` | Stable Hub map identifier |
| `map_label` | Human-readable map name |
| `map_type` | Flat, jumps, all-weather or unknown |
| `track_id` | Track identifier where present |
| `active` | Whether the map is currently usable |
| `valid_from`, `valid_to` | Known map validity interval |
| `source` | Hub table, report, KML or manual review |

Tasks:

- identify every map, including maps with generic labels such as `Default`;
- distinguish active, archived and superseded maps;
- identify multiple maps for one course;
- identify maps that represent different track layouts rather than duplicate records;
- determine whether the map is flat or jumps from Hub metadata, track metadata and report usage;
- retain `unknown` when the evidence is insufficient.

Deliverable: `data/config/jcr_maps.parquet`.

## 3. Inventory waypoints

Waypoints are map-specific. The configuration must not assume that waypoint 1 on one map is equivalent to waypoint 1 on another map.

| Field | Required meaning |
|---|---|
| `map_id` | Parent map |
| `waypoint_id` | Hub waypoint identifier, if available |
| `waypoint_number` | Number shown in the report or map |
| `waypoint_svg_id` | SVG identifier, if available |
| `label` | Human-readable label |
| `sequence` | Course order where known |
| `geometry_status` | KML, SVG, inferred or unavailable |
| `source` | Source table/file and review status |

Tasks:

- count configured waypoints per map;
- compare configured waypoints with observed GoingStick readings;
- detect duplicate waypoint numbers within a map;
- detect readings for unconfigured waypoints;
- record missing or unexpected waypoints without silently dropping them;
- keep waypoint numbers and Hub IDs as separate fields.

Deliverable: `data/config/jcr_waypoints.parquet` and a waypoint-compliance check table.

## 4. Model sections and overlapping zones

Sections and zones must be represented independently.

Recommended relationships:

```text
course 1 ───< map 1 ───< waypoint
                         ├──< waypoint_section >── section
                         └──< waypoint_zone >───── zone
```

The `waypoint_zone` table must allow multiple rows for the same waypoint and multiple zones to overlap. A zone should never be represented as a single exclusive category.

Required tables:

```text
sections(
  section_id, map_id, label, sequence, description, source
)

zones(
  zone_id, map_id, label, zone_type, description, source
)

waypoint_sections(
  map_id, waypoint_id, section_id, membership_source, confidence
)

waypoint_zones(
  map_id, waypoint_id, zone_id, membership_source, confidence
)
```

Tasks:

- extract Hub section and zone records;
- identify whether membership is explicit or inferred;
- preserve overlapping memberships;
- check for zones with no waypoints;
- check for waypoints with no section or zone;
- distinguish spatial zones from operational or reporting groups;
- record confidence and review notes for manual assignments.

Deliverable: four versioned configuration tables plus an overlap report.

## 5. Inventory and validate KML files

KML files provide spatial evidence for waypoint location, but availability and quality may vary by course and map.

For every candidate KML file:

- record the file path, checksum and date inspected;
- identify the course and map claimed by the file;
- extract waypoint names and longitude/latitude;
- normalise waypoint numbers;
- check for duplicate placemarks;
- check for missing configured waypoints;
- check for KML waypoints absent from the Hub configuration;
- record coordinate plausibility and geometry validity;
- link KML waypoints to Hub waypoints using explicit identifiers first.

KML status values:

```text
available_and_matched
available_partial_match
available_but_ambiguous
available_but_invalid
not_available
```

Do not spatially place a waypoint using nearest-neighbour matching without recording that it was inferred. Any inferred match requires a review flag.

Deliverable: `data/config/jcr_kml_inventory.parquet`, extracted KML waypoint tables and a KML validation report.

## 6. Import and validate SVG map assets

SVG assets are discovered from the imported Going Reports and their associated maps. Both waypoint and zone SVGs must be retained because they may contain different feature identifiers and visual information.

For every discovered SVG:

- record the source Going Report, map, course and document role;
- retain the original SVG text and a local copy where appropriate;
- calculate a SHA256 checksum and avoid re-downloading unchanged assets;
- parse elements with an `id`, preserving element name, class, style and labels;
- link SVG IDs to Hub waypoints, zones and sections where possible;
- record duplicate IDs, unmatched IDs, missing assets and parse errors;
- keep the original document even when parsing fails.

Recommended local datasets:

```text
svg_source_documents
svg_documents
svg_elements
```

SVG status values:

```text
retrieved_and_parsed
retrieved_parse_failed
not_available
source_report_not_imported
```

No SVG-dependent configuration check can pass while the relevant Going Reports remain unimported.

Deliverable: retained SVG assets, parsed SVG element tables and an SVG validation report.

## 7. Resolve map discipline and layout

Map discipline and layout determine which observations may be compared.

For each map, record:

```text
discipline = flat | jumps | all_weather | unknown
layout_label
map_role = primary | secondary | historical | unknown
comparison_group
evidence
confidence
```

For Cheltenham, explicitly investigate separate layouts such as Old Course and New Course, and retain hurdle/chase distinctions where the map metadata or Going Reports support them.

Acceptance rule: no cross-map comparison is allowed until the maps have either been assigned to a common comparison group or explicitly marked incomparable.

## 8. Create the configuration package

Create a versioned configuration package containing:

```text
config/
  jcr_courses.parquet
  jcr_maps.parquet
  jcr_waypoints.parquet
  jcr_sections.parquet
  jcr_zones.parquet
  jcr_waypoint_sections.parquet
  jcr_waypoint_zones.parquet
  jcr_kml_inventory.parquet
  jcr_svg_source_documents.parquet
  jcr_svg_documents.parquet
  jcr_svg_elements.parquet
  jcr_map_aliases.yml
  jcr_config_metadata.yml
```

`jcr_config_metadata.yml` should record:

- configuration version;
- extraction timestamp;
- database/schema version;
- source files and checksums;
- manual decisions;
- unresolved issues;
- reviewer and review date.

## 9. Run Phase 1 validation

The phase validation report must show:

| Check | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| Course scope | All 14 JCR courses identified or explicitly unresolved |
| Course IDs | No duplicate canonical course IDs |
| Maps | Every included course has at least one identified map or an exception |
| Map identity | No duplicate map IDs; archived maps flagged |
| Map discipline | Flat/jumps/unknown assigned with evidence |
| Waypoints | No silent loss of configured or observed waypoints |
| Sections | Section membership is map-specific |
| Zones | Overlapping zone membership is preserved |
| KML | Every file has a match status and checksum |
| Going Reports | All available reports imported or explicitly excepted |
| SVG | Every discovered asset has a retrieval and parse status |
| SVG matching | Waypoint, zone and section matches are quantified |
| Cheltenham | Maps, waypoints, sections, zones and KML status reviewed first |
| Provenance | Every manual decision has a source and confidence |

Phase 1 status should be `complete` only when all failed checks are either resolved or documented as accepted exceptions.

# Outputs and monitoring

## Required outputs

- configuration Parquet tables;
- YAML configuration and aliases;
- KML inventory and extracted coordinates;
- retained SVG assets and parsed SVG element tables;
- map/waypoint/zone/section validation report;
- Cheltenham configuration review;
- unresolved-issues register;
- this Quarto document rendered using the TurfTrax master template.

## Monitoring measures

The rendered document should report, by course and map:

- map count;
- active map count;
- waypoint count;
- section count;
- zone count;
- maximum zones per waypoint;
- percentage of waypoints with KML coordinates;
- percentage of observed waypoints configured;
- percentage of imported reports with discoverable SVG assets;
- percentage of SVG IDs matched to configured features;
- number of unresolved aliases;
- number of manual decisions;
- number of validation failures.

These measures become the baseline for later phases and should be rerun whenever the Hub schema, maps or KML resources change.

# Phase 1 acceptance decision

The phase review should end with one of three decisions:

```text
approved
approved_with_exceptions
not_approved
```

The approval record must name the exceptions that later phases may proceed with and those that block spatial analysis.

The next phase may begin only after the course and map identifiers are stable, the Cheltenham map hierarchy has been reviewed, and the configuration package has been versioned.
